apostles_creed.text:
I believe in God, the Father almighty,
Creator of heaven and earth,
and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord,
who was conceived by the Holy Spirit,
born of the Virgin Mary,
suffered under Pontius Pilate,
was crucified, died and was buried;
he descended into hell;
on the third day he rose again from the dead;
he ascended into heaven,
and is seated at the right hand of God the Father almighty;
from there he will come to judge the living and the dead.
I believe in the Holy Spirit,
the holy catholic Church,
the communion of saints,
the forgiveness of sins,
the resurrection of the body,
and life everlasting.
Amen.
apostles_creed.latin:
Credo in Deum Patrem omnipotentem,
Creatorem caeli et terrae,
et in Iesum Christum, Filium Eius unicum, Dominum nostrum,
qui conceptus est de Spiritu Sancto,
natus ex Maria Virgine,
passus sub Pontio Pilato,
crucifixus, mortuus, et sepultus,
descendit ad inferos,
tertia die resurrexit a mortuis,
ascendit ad caelos,
sedet ad dexteram Dei Patris omnipotentis,
inde venturus est iudicare vivos et mortuos.
Credo in Spiritum Sanctum,
sanctam Ecclesiam catholicam,
sanctorum communionem,
remissionem peccatorum,
carnis resurrectionem,
vitam aeternam.
Amen.

franciscan_crown_closing.text: O Mary, crowned with seven joys: by thy glad intercession obtain for us the grace to taste thy joys on earth, and to share them eternally in heaven. Amen.

hail_mary.text:
Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
Blessed art thou among women,
and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
Holy Mary, Mother of God,
pray for us sinners,
now and at the hour of our death.
Amen.
hail_mary.latin:
Ave Maria, gratia plena, Dominus tecum.
Benedicta tu in mulieribus,
et benedictus fructus ventris tui, Iesus.
Sancta Maria, Mater Dei,
ora pro nobis peccatoribus,
nunc et in hora mortis nostrae.
Amen.

schedule_note.note: The Franciscan Crown (Seraphic Rosary) in the received form of the Franciscan manuals: the Apostles’ Creed and Our Father, then seven decades of one Our Father and seven Hail Marys (one joy per decade, introduced after "Jesus" of each Hail Mary), concluding with two additional Hail Marys to complete the 72 years of tradition and a short original closing. The tradition crowns the joys especially on Saturdays, and during Lent substitutes the Seven Sorrows — see the pack’s "lent" documentation variant; the session ships the year-round joy form. The Catholic Encyclopedia’s recension with ten Hail Marys per decade is the alternate received form; the brief’s 7-Hail-Mary shape ships here.
schedule_note.structure: sign of the cross; Apostles’ Creed; Our Father; 7 decades of (1 Our Father + 7 Hail Marys); 2 additional Hail Marys; original closing
schedule_note.invocation_source: The Franciscan Crown (Seraphic Rosary; received 15th-century form)

variants.note: During Lent the tradition substitutes the Seven Sorrows of Our Lady for the Seven Joys (the crown of sorrows); the opening prayers and the two concluding Hail Marys remain. This pack ships the year-round joy form; the sorrows substitution is documented, not re-scheduled by the app.
